To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the participants initiated and constructed language learning sequences by transforming a cooking environment into a learning space.
students initiate and construct their own language-learning sequences by using the resources offered by the real-world environment, as well as by managing their own interaction with peers.

the learners initiate and construct language learning sequences in the digital cooking environment by using the material, semio- tical and interactional resources provided in the environment, and the peer interaction as means of knowledge-con- struction and interaction management.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ways in which learners can take control over their learning processes in a real-world environment, and how they can make use of their own interests and needs to create a learning environment that supports their language learning.

how learners can be encouraged to engage in self-initiated learning activities, and how the learning process can be supported by the material and interactional resources of a digital learning environment.
how students initiate, construct and navigate learning sequences in an informal, real-world digital environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the students’ activity and self-regulating behavior are not only a result of the learning environment, but also a product of their own initiative.
the participants’ own interests, needs and goals play a crucial role in the construction of language learning.
the participants are capable of constructing language-learning sequences without a language teacher in a real-world environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants’ language learning is not only initiated by them, but also sustained and supported by the digital environment and their peers.
students are able to initiate and sustain language-learning sequences in a real world digital environment without the guidance of a language teacher.
students can initiate and construct their own language-learning sequences, and that the digital environment provides them with the necessary resources to do so.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a language-learning activity that is initiated by students can be successfully embedded in a real-world environment that is not designed as a pedagogical setting, and that it can be supported by peer interaction and by the resources offered by the material and semiotic environment.
the design of digital learning environments should be informed by the pedagogical principles of self-regulated language learning.

a real-world digital learning environment provides a rich and varied context for language learning, and that the learners can use the environment and their own agency to construct learning sequences that are relevant to them and that are not limited by the pedagogical agenda of the teacher.
